name: Al-Qurashī inheritance fractions
summary: A Maghribi method credited to al-Qurashi split numbers into prime factors to find a common denominator for inheritance shares; al-Uqbani used it in a commentary by 1408.
description: A procedure attributed to al-Qurashī decomposes integers into prime factors to find a common denominator when calculating inheritance shares.
tier_reason: A particular inheritance procedure/commentary witness fits fine detail, with mathematical content distinct from the surviving report. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: A neater way to find common denominators, used by Maghribi inheritance calculators; a refinement of existing practice with no later work known to rest on it.

why: Dividing an estate under inheritance law meant adding and comparing many fractional shares, which needed a common denominator.

market.note: This node is scoped to mathematical knowledge and scholarly interpretation.

date.label: By 1408
date.basis: The named author died in 1408; the cited historian identifies the use in his commentary. The precise composition date is not established.

events.statement: Al-ʿUqbānī used al-Qurashī’s fraction method in his commentary on al-Hūfī by the end of his life in 1408.
events.caveats: Both accounts are by Ahmed Djebbar: his later article describes extensive teaching and application, while the earlier account says most legal practitioners continued an older method. Their geographic coverage and precise denominators are not established; the claims do not independently corroborate one another, and neither identifies a first use.

evidence.supports: Identifies the prime-factor method, names al-ʿUqbānī and al-Qalaṣādī as later expositors, and says many legal practitioners continued an older method.
